module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: Within the foundational finite support-state vocabulary, missing target-specific evidence blocks the authored promotion predicate, self-promotion is impossible, and terminal targets remain outside promotion.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Nine support-state labels, five transition effects, five propositional evidence fields, one legacy finite rank helper, terminal-state semantics, and narrow promotion predicates.
assumptions: The propositional evidence fields and state labels are truthful inputs.
RequiredEvidence is complete only for the declared finite vocabulary.
The legacy rank helper is not used to claim a total epistemic ordering among heterogeneous evidence categories.
countermodels: A target whose RequiredEvidence proposition is false cannot satisfy PromotionAllowed.
No state can promote to itself because the finite rank relation is irreflexive.
Deprecated and refuted targets cannot satisfy the authored promotion predicate.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: The projection-aware consumer supplies target-evidence and authority mutations; the cluster validator mutates module identity, proposition, countermodels, consumers, and inference ceilings.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Retain only as a narrow foundational vocabulary and deductive blocker. It does not establish a total confidence ladder, evidence truth, reviewer competence, source interpretation, artifact validity, open-world soundness, runtime enforcement, or support movement.

module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: A claim-specific transition can reach bounded ledger handoff only through exact atom and proposition/obligation/predicate custody, target-specific non-aggregating evidence, adverse-transition burden, review, dissent, limitations, residuals, and changelog records, without direct support, inherited movement, or external-effect authority.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Six reachable stages, thirty-five routes, exact atom and three-projection digests, heterogeneous target-evidence dimensions, adverse-transition semantics, review, decision, handoff, acknowledgment, and explicit authority exclusions.
assumptions: Digests, evidence fields, review records, and intent labels are truthful inputs.
Digest equality does not itself establish semantic equivalence among the three projections.
The route ordering is the declared finite policy for one claim-specific transition.
countermodels: Atom or projection substitution, event replay, terminal-intent mismatch, and state substitution are rejected.
Missing target evidence or adverse-transition negative evidence, trigger, and supersession records block evidence binding.
Support assignment, parent or descendant movement, and external-effect requests never reach an accepted route.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: The independent consumer reaches all 35 declared routes, including 35 rejecting identity, evidence, review, decision, handoff, replay, inheritance, support, and effect cases.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Adequate for the represented finite projection-aware transition-control boundary. It does not establish evidence truth, projection equivalence, reviewer independence, a correct live support decision, inherited movement, release readiness, or external effects.

module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: A single-claim append-only revision lifecycle preserves exact claim identity, zero external effects, and exact ledger-version/append-count balance across arbitrary successful event lists, admits an append only from an exact base matching the full pending proposal and evidence-owner custody, composes event batches, and reaches a terminal surface acknowledgment only after exact materialization.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Five lifecycle stages, twenty-two route cases, immutable claim identity, semantic and ontology versions, head and append counts, full pending proposal, contradiction state, evidence-owner receipt, history, dependency, residual, migration, materialized view, and surface acknowledgment.
assumptions: Identifiers, digests, evidence-owner receipts, dependencies, migrations, and surface acknowledgments are truthful.
Digest collision resistance and concurrent event-store behavior are outside the model.
The route fields are sufficient for this single-claim lifecycle.
countermodels: A stale base or ledger self-approval is rejected.
Upward revision with an open contradiction is blocked; missing evidence-owner custody is handed off rather than accepted.
Ontology change without migration custody and acknowledgment before materialization are rejected.
Five same-digest substitutions of action, semantic version, ontology version, support rank, or evidence-owner receipt are rejected.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: The independent consumer compiles the exact theorem surface, covers all 22 route cases, consumes the 5/7 revision fixtures and 1/11 historical lifecycle, and rejects 34 identity, version, same-digest payload, history, contradiction, ownership, migration, surface, order, and acknowledgment mutations.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Adequate for the represented reachable append-only lifecycle, route priority, arbitrary-run identity and history custody, exact append accounting, proposal-payload commitment, batch composition, terminal closure, and authority separation. It does not establish natural claim extraction, semantic equivalence, evidence or reviewer quality, contradiction discovery, concurrency, persistence, causal benefit, transfer, or chapter-core support.

module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: A frozen claim target can move through artifact binding, verifier execution, bounded adjudication, and owner writeback only with exact target, interpretation, artifact, verifier, trusted-base, attempt-history, semantic-review, dossier, dissent, limitation, residual, and authority custody; accepted steps preserve identity, add one receipt, and cannot assign support or an external effect.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Six stages, twenty-three routes, exact target and artifact bindings, verifier result distinct from semantic adequacy, risk and tribunal requirements, attempt history, dissent, limitations, residuals, owner handoff, receipt count, support-assignment count, and external-effect count.
assumptions: Identifiers, digests, artifact presence, verifier result, semantic review, trusted base, dossier quality, and owner receipt are truthful inputs.
Verifier soundness, reviewer independence, and semantic equivalence are not derived.
The route ordering is the declared policy for one verification event.
countermodels: A passed verifier without artifact references and a negative result without attempt history are rejected.
A negative result cannot propose promotion, and a mismatch cannot bypass tribunal effect.
An unverified pass, high-risk result without an independent dossier, or writeback requesting support assignment is blocked.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: The independent consumer covers all 23 routes, consumes 3/5 proof fixtures and 2/7 adversarial-dossier cases, and rejects 36 target, interpretation, artifact, verifier, result, dossier, dissent, limitation, residual, writeback, support, and effect mutations.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Adequate for the represented target-specific verification lifecycle, binding custody, negative-result handling, receipt accounting, and authority separation. It does not establish target interpretation, artifact or source truth, proof or verifier soundness, reviewer competence or independence, verdict quality, claim truth, useful outcomes, safety, transfer, or chapter-core support.

module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: Within the finite proof-envelope record, contradictions rule out implemented status when a module is missing or a build failed, non-Lean artifacts cannot be labeled Lean proofs, support promotion is invalid without an accepted transition and bounded semantic and non-claim records, and external theorem references require exact identity and scope boundaries.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Proof-target status with module/build flags plus artifact lane, verifier result, semantic-adequacy label, support-effect request, accepted-transition flag, consumer match, limitations, non-claims, and external theorem identity fields.
assumptions: All record fields are truthful and the bounded predicates are complete for the declared admission decision.
Module existence, build success, theorem semantics, external theorem identity, and consumer effects are not checked by Lean itself.
The two former direct positive projections have been retired; the retained declarations are bounded negative cases or derived countermodels over the finite record.
countermodels: Implemented status with a missing module or failing build contradicts ImplementedTargetValid.
A non-Lean artifact carrying a Lean-proof claim is rejected.
Support promotion without transition, adequate finite semantics, limitations, non-claims, or consumer match is rejected; external references without identifiers or boundaries are rejected.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: Repository proof-readiness and artifact-audit validators exercise the executable manifest surface and bind the retained bounded countermodel theorem names; this cluster validator rejects missing module, countermodel, consumer, and maximum-inference records. There is no checked Lean-to-runtime refinement, and the former positive projection theorems are retired rather than credited as enforcement.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Retain only as finite proof-artifact admission countermodels and specification-layer policy. It does not establish that files exist, builds ran, theorems are true or semantically adequate, external references resolve, support transitions are enforced, consumers obey the envelope, or any empirical or safety claim holds.

cluster_maximum_inference: The cluster is adequate at bounded finite custody semantics after retiring the direct ProofEnvelope projections and retaining only consumed countermodels and bounded non-executable rules. It proves no claim truth, evidence truth, verifier soundness, reviewer quality, deployed enforcement, empirical behavior, safety, transfer, SOTA, AGI, ASI, or support-state movement.
